statement.p: Which of the following decompositions of f(x) = p (q(x) ) into a pair of functions p(x) (the outside function) and q(x) (the inside function) is/are correct ? Select all that apply if more than one is appropriate.

static.solution:
SOLUTION
There is often many (even infinite) ways to decompose a given function into a suitable pair of inside and outside functions. In this case, the following decompositions work: \begin{aligned} p(x) = \sqrt{x},\amp \qquad q(x) = 9 - 2 x \\ p(x) = \sqrt{9 - x}\amp \qquad q(x) = 2 x \\ p(x) = \sqrt{-x} \amp \qquad q(x) = 2 x - 9 \end{aligned}
The other choices do not work since:
If p(x) = 9 - 2 x and q(x) = \sqrt{x}, then p(q(x)) = 9 - 2 \sqrt{x} \ne f(x).
if p(x) = \sqrt{9 + x} and q(x) = 2 x, then p(q(x)) = \sqrt{9+2 x} \ne f(x).
if p(x) = \sqrt{- 2 x} and \ q(x) = 9 + x, then p(q(x)) = \sqrt{-2 x - 18} \ne f(x).
